section.title: Finding the Curve of Best Fit
section.para: Let's find the curve of best fit for a given data set.
Use the Desmos graphing tool to determine the equation.
Step 1 - Click the + symbol in the top left and select a table.
Enter the data set as shown. Press Enter.
The data set will populate the graph as shown here.

Step 2
On the left side, click in box #2 for a new item. Enter the instruction line below to generate a curve of best fit.

list.item: Remember from the activity that Desmos will automatically place the 1 as subscript after an \(x\) or \(y\).
Don't forget to use the symbol ~ that means approximately.
Use the ^ symbol to enter an exponent.

section.para: As soon as you enter the instruction line, Desmos will generate the curve of best fit.
Step 3 - Use the coefficients generated to write the equation for the curve of best fit.

image.alt: OUTPUT SUMMARY FOR A QUADRATIC REGRESSION. R-SQUARED IS 0.9958. A, B, AND C ARE NEGATIVE 2.75569, 37.0352, AND 65.6605, RESPECTIVELY.

section.para: Round each coefficient to the nearest hundredth.
The curve of best fit is \(y = -2.76x^2+ 37.04x + 65.66\).
section.title: Try It: Finding the Curve of Best Fit
section.para: Find the equation of the curve of best fit. Round each coefficient to the nearest hundredth.

problem.para: Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to find the curve of best fit:
Solve for the curve of best fit by entering \(y_1 \sim ax_1^2+bx_1+ c\).
The curve of best fit is \(y = 6.18x^2+ 4.59x + 25.42\).
